A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARMOR and ARMOR-Think work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and matchable despite formatting changes and table relocation.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original jailbreak, safety, utility, ablation, and additional base-model evaluation results.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a controlled experiment withholding three jailbreak strategies during training.

M1.justification: The three-stage reasoning pipeline, dynamic strategy library, SFT, step-wise DPO, PRM-based inference, and ARMOR-Think construction remain unchanged. The new experiment evaluates the existing method under restricted training exposure.

E1.justification: The training sources, safety and utility benchmarks, and four strategy-based attacks are retained. The new Appendix C experiment uses three strategies already represented in v2’s training coverage and library; its withholding control changes experimental design within existing jailbreak-defense coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Qwen-2.5, STAR, and STAIR comparisons in the controlled unseen-strategy experiment in Table 14. These existing baseline families expand the strategy-generalization comparison beyond the ARMOR-only configurations in the retained Table 6; existing comparator memberships remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds retraining after excluding Coded Language Obfuscation, Role-Based Compliance Priming, and Format-Based Obfuscation, accounting for 20.7% of strategy-based training samples. Evaluation compares seen-strategy, unseen-strategy, and inference-time library-update conditions. Previously reported settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 14 tests dependence on training exposure to particular strategies and whether supplying the excluded strategies at inference restores safety. This extends the existing component ablations and four-attack extrapolation analysis with a targeted control.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added Table 14 follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. New Table 14 reports ARMOR unseen-strategy rates of 0.04, 0.02, and 0.04 for the three listed strategies, versus 0.00, 0.01, and 0.00 after library updates. These are additional controlled-experiment results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, the DPO objective, ternary reward definitions, and threat-model assumptions are retained. The new appendix discussion introduces no formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same method, safety, utility, and rapid-adaptation claims, including average harmfulness of 0.002 and attack success rate of 0.06. The additional experiment supplies evidence for an existing generalization claim.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds an explanation of withheld-strategy performance: the library provides background knowledge, while recognizing shared obfuscation patterns supports intent extraction without strategy-specific training exposure. The existing inference-overhead limitation and broader-impact discussion are relocated without substantive changes.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 changes the access pointer from the project website to the ARMOR code repository. Appendix C documents the excluded strategies and their 20.7% training-data share. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Author–year citations replace numbered citations, with corresponding bibliography formatting changes but no substantive addition or removal of related work.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations and publication headers, adds acknowledgments and an LLM usage statement, and moves Limitations and Broader Impact after the references. It expands Appendix C while retaining most existing prose and the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 14, relocates existing appendix tables, and renumbers subsequent tables. The ICLR template changes title, heading, header, and page-flow presentation. Figures 1–8 and existing table displays are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: The added Appendix C experiment strengthens the existing generalization argument through explicit strategy withholding and inference-time restoration controls, supplementing v2’s Table 6. The gain is limited: the new evaluation does not specify its sample count or report uncertainty, and the main methods and results remain unchanged.
